title: cafaye metric signal
description: What a cafaye metric is permitted to carry, and the hard prohibition this schema exists to enforce. OpenTelemetry caps aggregation at 2000 distinct attribute combinations per metric stream; on overflow the SDK folds everything into a single point carrying otel.metric.overflow=true and DROPS ALL MEASUREMENT ATTRIBUTES. Totals remain correct and every per-dimension breakdown silently undercounts. That is the worst shape a bug can have: the dashboard still renders, the total still looks right, and the breakdown is wrong, with no error anywhere. So `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `account_id`, `request_id`, `trace_id` and every other unbounded identifier are prohibited here and required on `resourceAttributes` instead, which are attached once per process, are exempt from the cap, and stay queryable on the overflow point. The two attribute maps are disjoint by construction: a name on the resource list cannot be used as a measurement attribute even if someone adds it to the allowlist, and `additionalProperties: false` means a name on neither list is a failure rather than a silent new dimension. See docs/observability.md.

name.description: The metric name, dotted and lowercase, conventionally `<namespace>.<subject>.<unit>`. The same shape discipline as span names and for the same reason: a name that embeds a value is a stream per value.

unit.description: The UCUM unit, from a closed list. cafaye's money is integer minor units and never a metric, so there is no currency unit here on purpose.

description.description: One line on what the number means. Required, because a metric with no stated meaning is a number in a dashboard nobody dares delete and nobody can explain.

measurementAttributes.description: The dimensions of the measurement. Every value here multiplies against every other, so the set is a closed list of bounded dimensions and the product of their cardinalities is a design-time budget a reviewer can do in their head.

resourceAttributes.description: Identity, attached once per process. This is where `tenant_id` and `account_id` go; the prohibition above is a prohibition with a destination, and this is the destination.

measurementAttributes.description: The complete set of measurement dimensions a cafaye metric may carry. Every entry is bounded — an enum, a length cap, or a small range — because an unbounded dimension is a stream per value, and 2000 combinations is where the SDK starts folding. `error.type` is the sharpest case: it is the one dimension that sounds like a classification and behaves like an identifier if it is left free. Unbounded identifiers are excluded twice over: they are not on this list, and `not` refuses them by name so that adding one to the list later does not quietly succeed.

http.request.method.description: Eight values. A safe dimension, and the model every other attribute on this list is measured against.

http.route.description: The ROUTE TEMPLATE, never the concrete path. One value per endpoint, not one per request — which is the entire difference between a usable metric and a cardinality bomb. The `{id}` in `/v1/users/{id}` is what makes it bounded; the same route with the id filled in is not on this list.

http.response.status_code_class.description: The status CLASS, four values, not the code. Deliberately coarser than the traces signal's `http.response.status_code`: a metric multiplied by 500 status codes and every route is how a 2000-combination cap is reached in a week, and `4xx` answers the question a dashboard actually asks.

db.operation.description: Six values. A closed verb vocabulary, never the statement text.

error.type.description: The error CLASS, and the reason the fleet's errors are aggregatable in one place rather than being a wall of ungrouped text. **Closed vocabulary, not a shape** — and on THIS signal the difference is the whole point of the attribute, because an unbounded dimension on a metric is exactly the failure this schema exists to prevent. A `pattern` bounds the shape of the value and not the set of values, so `user_42_email_invalid` validated cleanly: snake_case, twenty-two characters, and one series per value. That is `tenant_id` on a measurement under a name that sounds like a classification. Byte-identical to the same `enum` in traces.schema.json and logs.schema.json, because the class recorded here must be **identical** to the class on the span for the same operation — and a rule comparing two documents is only enforceable if both sides draw from one list. The twelve classes and the fallback: D18 says why each earns its place, D14 is the granularity call this implements, D19 is why the OTel fallback `_OTHER` is in a snake_case vocabulary (it exists so instrumentation is never forced to invent a class, and an alert on `_OTHER` is an alert that this service has not classified its own errors). `pattern` and `maxLength` are the second line, not the rule: they cannot reject a value the `enum` accepts. `error.message` is prohibited by name in the `not` above and is never to be added: a provider's content-policy rejection quotes the offending content back, so the message is a prompt by another route, and on this signal it would also be an unbounded dimension. This dimension is required on the operation duration histogram — that is how error rate is computable without a message in a label — and **absent on success**, which is why the absence is load-bearing rather than an omission. Handled and retried errors are not recorded here at all: `SHOULD NOT` in semconv, because a retry that succeeded is not an error and recording it makes the error rate a lie. `_OTHER` and the other eleven classes are Development-stability-adjacent: `error.type` itself is Stable, the cross-signal coupling in `recording-errors.md` is not (D18).

resourceAttributes.description: Identity, attached once per process rather than per measurement. This is the destination the prohibition points at, and the reason is mechanical: resource attributes are not part of the attribute set the 2000-combination cap counts, so they are exempt from it and they survive on the overflow point — which means a per-tenant total stays answerable even when the measurement has folded. Disjoint from `measurementAttributes` by construction; tests/test_specs.py asserts no name appears on both lists.

service.namespace.description: The grouping this service belongs to — `cafaye` for every one of them. Stable in the OTel semantic conventions and the documented companion to `service.name`: it is what lets one collector group the fleet under a parent instead of showing seven unrelated services. muse sets it by hand (`src/muse/telemetry.py:390`) and is the only publisher that does, which is why it was missing here and why the list being closed cost a real span a validation it should have passed.

telemetry.sdk.name.description: Which SDK built this process's metrics — `opentelemetry` in every language here. Stable semconv, and **not** an optional embellishment: billing sets it by hand at `lib/kit/telemetry.rb:183`, and the Python SDK's `Resource.create/1` merges it from its own default resource whether or not the caller asked. A service cannot suppress it without opting out of the SDK's defaults, so a resource allowlist without it does not describe a metric — it describes the publishers whose resource is built without one.

telemetry.sdk.language.description: The implementation language, from the same two places as `telemetry.sdk.name`, and load-bearing for the same reason: a metric that says which runtime produced it is what tells an operator that a fleet with four languages has four resource shapes. identity — the only service in the fleet that exports metrics, and one that builds its resource with Go's schemaless `resource.NewWithAttributes` — reports none of these three.

telemetry.sdk.version.description: The SDK's own version — the fact that distinguishes two metric streams this spec cannot otherwise tell apart, since both satisfy every constraint above. Bounded to one value per process, like every other resource attribute, which is why it belongs here rather than on a measurement.

tenant_id.description: PROHIBITED as a measurement attribute, REQUIRED here. Unbounded as a dimension; exempt as a resource, and queryable on every point including the overflow one.

account_id.description: Same reasoning as tenant_id. The cafe is multi-tenant, so these two are the values a careless implementation reaches for first.
